not_covered: Anthropic released the Claude 4 family on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch included two distinct models to serve different market segments and use cases:

*   **Claude Opus 4:** Positioned as the flagship model ("Claude 4"), it was priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

*   **Claude Sonnet 4:** Positioned as a "fast workhorse" and the developer-default coding model, it was significantly cheaper at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The decision to release these specific tiers signaled that Anthropic viewed agentic coding as its primary competitive battleground against OpenAI’s o-series in an enterprise "agentic-coding gold rush" [Source: ev-1].

By highlighting capabilities such as "computer use 2.0," which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation's browser control (referenced as the 3.x generation), Anthropic positioned Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent available [Source: ev-1].

This strategy aimed to capture both high-end performance needs with Opus and volume-driven developer adoption with Sonnet, a move that contributed to record API usage and helped cement Anthropic’s position as a leader in the coding-agent market [Source: ev-1].

The evidence also notes subsequent developments related to this launch context:
*   A **4.1** update released on June 18, 2025, improved coding and agentic reliability at the same prices; the naming ("4.1" rather than "4.5") followed a reported internal dispute about version-naming policy [Source: ev-1].
*   Driven by Claude Code adoption (the defining agentic-coding product of 2025), Anthropic raised a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported ~$183 billion valuation [Source: ev-1].
